defaultProfile.description:
THE PROFILE THE LAPTOP COMES UP IN: "quiet" | "balanced" | "performance", or null (the default: nothing stored, the
profile is whatever the firmware comes up in). Named here, it holds FROM EARLY BOOT, before the login screen: the shell
stores that profile's row of "profiles" below as the root helper's boot set (`set-boot`, /var/lib/silicon/boot.json),
and silicon-boot.service applies the set at every boot. The shell never changes the profile when it starts: an edit here
is stored within a second and takes effect at the NEXT boot (the profile in use now stays until you switch). Editing the
named profile's row stores its new values too. Taking the key out stores nothing and clears nothing -- the last stored
set stays in force; to clear it (the charge limit is kept):
    pkexec /usr/local/libexec/silicon-helper set-boot

Takes "quiet", "balanced" or "performance" or null. Default: null.

profiles.description:
WHAT A PROFILE APPLIES. Switching profile (the popup's arrows, a swipe, or a change made
outside it) sets the platform profile -- the embedded controller's thermal policy: fans,
and whatever the firmware enforces -- and then these values, which the firmware never moves
by itself. A value left `null` means "keep the firmware's value":
  maxPerfPct, pl1W, pl2W   the kernel's maximum / the ceiling the firmware set at boot, written
                           on every switch, so a switch ends a tweak of them;
  epp, turbo, governor     not written at all (a tweak of those survives a switch).
Energy preference `epp`: power | balance_power | balance_performance | performance.
`turbo`: true | false. `governor`: powersave | performance (| schedutil ... where the kernel
offers them). `maxPerfPct`: 1..100, a whole percent of the maximum performance.
`pl1W`, `pl2W`: the sustained and the burst package power limit in watts, 1..400; the helper
only ever LOWERS them (floor 8 W, ceiling the firmware's own values: 45 W / 115 W here), on
both RAPL interfaces, with PL1 <= PL2.

onPower.description:
THE PROFILE BY POWER: the profile to switch to when the charger goes in ("ac") and when it comes out ("battery"); null = none. Only the
plug switches: a profile you pick stays until the next plug, nothing is switched at the shell's start, and a system update's hold
goes first (the profile is what comes back after it).

holds.description: While a system update runs the CPU is held at: "performance" | "balanced" | null (not at all).

battery.description:
The battery is low from this percentage down (of the pack the charge limit leaves): the bar's figure turns red and the OSD's card
comes. 5 .. 50. (The toasts' levels are notifications.jsonc sources.battery.)

guard.description: Takes true or false. Default: true.

resumeKick.description: Takes true or false. Default: true.

fans.description:
The fan guard (a CPU hotter than its load explains: a card, and Performance held), and the fans' wake-up after a resume. Both answer a fault of this
laptop's firmware. true | false.

sounds.description:
The popup's sounds. How loud they are is the mockup's. true | false.

Takes true or false. Default: true.

interactionBoost.description:
THE INTERACTION BOOST: while a motion of the shell runs (a popup opening, the island moving: a few hundred ms) the shell asks
lares-boost.service to hold the Intel GPU's and the CPU's frequency floor up, and the service puts both back by itself. A motion
otherwise ends before the hardware has woken from its rest (800 MHz GPU, 400 MHz cores on quiet). Needs the root service (`lares
setup`, step R6); without it this does nothing. Off by default: measure it first (docs/silicon.md "The interaction boost").
The floors themselves are the service's (its unit's gpuMhz / cpuPct). true | false.

Takes true or false. Default: false.

overhead.description:
WHAT THE POPUP COSTS. Watts per second of the shell's CPU time and of its GPU render time,
used to show the battery's draw WITHOUT the popup's own (hover shows the real figure). These
are uncalibrated seeds (tools/silicon/calibrate_overhead.sh measures this machine's); 0 .. 50, 0 turns the correction off.

askWhenBusy.description:
Switching to Integrated or Smart asks first while an app is on the card. false: it switches (the apps keep running).

Takes true or false. Default: true.

blockedNotice.description:
A card when an app was kept off the card.

Takes true or false. Default: true.

ignoredHolders.description: Takes a list of texts. Default: ["cardwired","nvidia-persiste","nvidia-persistenced","hyprland","xwayland","xorg","systemd","systemd-logind","btop","nvidia-smi","quickshell"].

gpu.description:
THE dGPU's USERS THE POPUP DOES NOT ASK ABOUT. Switching to Integrated or Smart with an app on the NVIDIA card asks first (the apps keep
running; cardwire only blocks NEW opens). A process listed here never counts as an app on the card: not for that question, not for the
"in use by" line, not for the nvidia-smi gate. Names are the process's own (the kernel's `comm`, 15 characters at most), matched whole
and without regard to case. The list is the whole truth: take Hyprland out and it is a user again. The default is the plumbing that
holds the card's nodes while it sleeps -- cardwired and nvidia-persistenced, the session (Hyprland, Xwayland, Xorg, systemd,
systemd-logind), the shell itself (quickshell), and the programs that only WATCH the card -- btop and nvidia-smi (they keep it out of
D3cold while they run, which is fine; the shell's own nvidia-smi queries count here too, and counting them made the shell its own user).

look.description:
THE LOOK of the board: "family" is "material" (carved; the old "eva" still works) or "blueprint"; "secondarySide" is WHERE THE POPUP'S SECONDARIES OPEN --
the CPU tuning and GPU panels and the three dialogs (the restart card, the keep prompt, the question about apps on the dGPU):
"far" (away from the bar), or "start" / "end" (along it). The mockup's panel tries them live. How LARGE the popup is drawn is
shell.jsonc's "scale": { "popups": { "silicon": 1.35 } }.
